finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /rss passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open, so the server fetches any URL the attacker names. This includes internal services, loopback, and cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/. open-uri also follows redirects, and it supports http, https and ftp. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a read SSRF.

trace.note: get "/rss" route has no auth guard
params[:u] is passed unvalidated to URI.open (open-uri), which fetches the URL
first 400 bytes of the response body are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, or private/loopback/link-local IP blocking. No redirect restrictions. No authentication on the route. The TRUSTED allowlist at line 5 is applied only to /trusted, not here.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] from the unauthenticated GET /rss route (app.rb:7) directly to URI.open with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes; the TRUSTED check at app.rb:14 only guards /trusted, and no other files or middleware exist.
